descriptionChirho: A Canaanite place name (אֲפֵק / אֲפִיק), meaning perhaps 'enclosure' or 'fortress,' applied to several cities in the land of Israel. The name appears with various spellings: Aphek (Josh 12:18, 1 Sam 29:1), Aphekah (Josh 13:4 in the hill country of Judah), Afeqah (1 Kgs 20:26, 20:30 near the Golan), and Afik (Judg 1:31, the Asherite city). All forms refer to fortified Canaanite sites, and the different spellings (with or without he locale suffix -ah) and prepositional prefixes (בַאֲפֵק 'in Aphek,' וַאֲפֵק 'and Aphek') are purely orthographic and grammatical variants of the same toponym. Glosses across all languages consistently transliterate the name: arb أَفيق, deu Aphek, spa Afec, kor 아벡/아벡.
